title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sets up the iterated relative Frobenius and its trace, to be used for the Cartier operator and Hasse–Witt action on the Hodge bundle.

1. Setting. S is a scheme of characteristic p and X/S a scheme with the usual conditions from the previous page (X → X^{(p/S)} flat, X/S locally of finite presentation, in practice X/S smooth with Ω^1 locally free). The relative Frobenius is f_{X/S} : X → X^{(p/S)}, where X^{(p/S)} = X ×_{S,F_S} S.

2. Iteration. Base-changing f_{X/S} along F_S^i gives f^{(p^i)}_{X/S} : X^{(p^i/S)} → X^{(p^{i+1}/S)}. Composing these gives the ν-fold relative Frobenius F^{(ν)}_{X/S} = f^{(p^{ν-1})} ∘ … ∘ f : X → X^{(p^ν/S)}. This is the relative Frobenius for the absolute Frobenius power F_S^ν.

3. Trace on differentials. Now take X/S smooth of relative dimension 1 (a relative curve). Since F^{(ν)}_{X/S} is finite and flat, it has a trace (Gysin / duality) map on top-degree forms, Tr : F^{(ν)}_* Ω^1_{X/S} → Ω^1_{X^{(p^ν)}/S}. Pushing forward by the structure maps g_0 : X → S and g_ν : X^{(p^ν)} → S gives (F^{(ν)})_* : g_{0*}Ω^1_{X/S} → g_{ν*}Ω^1_{X^{(p^ν)}/S}.

4. Base change. Formation of g_*Ω^1 commutes with base change for smooth proper curves, so the target is identified with F_S^{ν*}ω = ω^{(p^ν)}, where ω = g_{0*}Ω^1_{X/S} is the Hodge bundle. One therefore gets a p^{-ν}-linear Cartier map ω → ω^{(p^ν)}, which is the iterated Cartier operator on the Hodge bundle; for ν = 1 its matrix is the Cartier–Manin (Hasse–Witt transpose) matrix.

5. The case F_S^ν = id. If λ ↦ λ^{p^ν} is the identity on O_S (e.g. S over F_{p^ν}), then X^{(p^ν/S)} ≅ X canonically. In that case F^{(ν)}_{X/S} is an S-endomorphism of X, namely the ν-th iterate F_X^ν of absolute Frobenius, so the trace gives a linear endomorphism of ω.

6. General S. In general the composite X → X^{(p^ν/S)} → X (the second map is the canonical projection, lying over F_S^ν : S → S) equals the absolute Frobenius F_X^ν.

7. Purpose. The next page (crossed out) starts to specialize to S = Spec F_p, with F_X acting on ω. The goal is to relate the Cartier operator / Hasse–Witt matrix to the Gauss–Manin connection and Picard–Fuchs equations (cf. Katz's later work and Dwork-style congruences). All statements are standard and correct.
errors: Minor notation: the page writes both F^{(ν)}_{X/S} and F^{ν}_{X/S} for the same map, and the iterate superscripts are p^{i}/S versus p^{(i)}. No mathematical error.
The identification of g_{ν*}Ω^1 with ω^{(p^ν)} needs base change for g_*Ω^1. This holds for smooth proper curves, but is left implicit on the page (via the 'dualité/degré de base' remark).

ideas.what: Iterated relative Frobenius X → X^{(p^ν/S)} as a composite of base-changed relative Frobenii, and its factorization of absolute Frobenius F_X^ν over F_S^ν

deep.surprise_reason: Routine setup of the iterated relative Frobenius and the trace/Cartier operator on the Hodge bundle of a relative curve. Everything is standard, foundational material for the Gauss–Manin/Cartier comparison developed in the published literature.
transcription_corrections: The word under 'Tr' transcribed as 'Grothendieck [?]' looks more like 'Gysin', i.e. the trace is identified with the Gysin map.
'f_{X/S}' is written in fraktur, i.e. 𝔣_{X/S}; in the composite the factors are 𝔣^{(p^{ν-1})}_{X/S} 𝔣^{(p^{ν-2})}_{X/S} … 𝔣_{X/S}.
The struck-out symbol before '∑ f_*' reads 'X^{p^ν}' (crossed out); the following term is g_{ν*}(Ω^1_{X^{(p^ν)}/S}).
The parenthetical phrase '(via dualité de faisceaux de degré de base)' is uncertain in the image; the readable sense is an identification compatible with base change.
The duplicated line 'que par hyp. F_S^ν = id_S, on voit que F_X^ν est' is a transcription repetition; the page has it once: 'car par hyp. F_S^ν = id_S, on voit que F_X^ν est bien un S-endomorphisme'.
